{
  "research_question": "Do stimulation paradigms (Combined, ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only, Sham) differentially affect mouse navigation performance as measured by Time-to-Target, Success, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, and Angular Dispersion (AD)?",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Combined", "ICMS Only", "Dim Visual Only", "Bright Visual Only", "Sham"],
  "response_variables": ["Time-to-Target", "Success", "Path Efficiency", "Average Speed", "AD"],
  "anova_plan": [
    "Time-to-Target: One-way ANOVA with Stim Paradigm as fixed factor. The data show substantial right skew (max=201.39 vs mean=2.81) and potential outliers. Consider log-transformation or robust ANOVA. Alternative: Kruskal-Wallis test if normality severely violated.",
    "Success: Binary outcome (0/1) with mean 0.73. Standard ANOVA inappropriate. Use logistic regression with Stim Paradigm as categorical predictor, or chi-square test of independence, or Cochran's Q if repeated measures structure emphasized. Report odds ratios relative to Sham baseline.",
    "Path Efficiency: One-way ANOVA with Stim Paradigm. Extreme right skew evident (max=29.82, mean=0.47, sd=0.47). Log-transformation strongly recommended. Alternative: Kruskal-Wallis or permutation ANOVA.",
    "Average Speed: One-way ANOVA with Stim Paradigm. Moderate right tail (max=75.35, mean=12.50). Check normality; may need transformation or robust methods.",
    "AD (Angular Dispersion): One-way ANOVA with Stim Paradigm. Bounded [0,1] variable with mean 0.38, sd 0.24. Beta regression or arcsine-square-root transformation recommended due to bounded support. Standard ANOVA may yield predictions outside [0,1]."
  ],
  "assumptions_and_diagnostics": [
    "Independence: Violated - 76,655 trials nested within 8 mice (7,233-10,986 trials per mouse). Mouse-specific clustering requires mixed-effects models or mouse as blocking factor.",
    "Normality: QQ plots and Shapiro-Wilk tests for residuals required. Time-to-Target, Path Efficiency severely non-normal; AD bounded; Success binary.",
    "Homoscedasticity: Levene's test across paradigms. Visual inspection of group SDs suggests variance heterogeneity (e.g., Sham Success SD=0.45 vs Combined=0.41 from summary).",
    "Sample size imbalance: Combined dominates (48,846/76,655=63.7%), Sham smallest (3,505=4.6%). Weighted analyses or careful interpretation of unbalanced designs needed.",
    "Repeated measures: Same mice across paradigms (within-subject design). Standard one-way ANOVA ignores this; linear mixed model with Mouse as random intercept preferred."
  ],
  "posthoc_plan": [
    "If omnibus test significant: Pairwise comparisons with Tukey HSD (or Tukey-Kramer for unequal n) for continuous variables, with Benjamini-Hochberg or Bonferroni correction for multiple comparisons.",
    "For Success (logistic): Pairwise odds ratios with Holm-Bonferroni correction. Focus on Sham vs active stimulation contrasts.",
    "Planned contrasts: Combined vs single-modality conditions (ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only) to test multisensory integration hypothesis; active vs Sham for efficacy.",
    "Effect sizes: Cohen's d or Hedges' g for continuous variables; odds ratios for Success; partial eta-squared for omnibus tests."
  ],
  "expected_findings": [
    "Sham expected to show poorest performance: lowest Success (0.273), highest Time-to-Target (4.68s), lowest Path Efficiency (0.308), lowest Average Speed (10.74), lowest AD (0.236).",
    "Combined stimulation expected superior: highest Success (0.780), lowest Time-to-Target (2.56s), high Path Efficiency (0.502), highest Average Speed (12.83), highest AD (0.399).",
    "Visual-only paradigms: Bright Visual Only > Dim Visual Only on Success (0.785 vs 0.673), Time-to-Target (2.61s vs 3.14s), Path Efficiency (0.504 vs 0.434), AD (0.387 vs 0.336).",
    "ICMS Only intermediate: Success 0.685, Time-to-Target 3.05s—suggesting unisensory ICMS less effective than combined or bright visual but better than dim visual or sham.",
    "Mouse-by-paradigm interactions likely: SC11LM shows extreme Sham impairment (Success 0.067) vs SC11L1RF (Sham Success 0.245), indicating individual differences in baseline or stimulation response."
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "Severe imbalance in paradigm frequencies (Combined 63.7% of data) reduces precision for rare conditions, especially Sham (4.6%).",
    "No trial-level temporal information (learning effects, session effects) available in artifacts.",
    "Path Efficiency shows extreme outliers (max=29.8, 99th percentile likely <<5), suggesting calculation artifacts or rare events.",
    "Mouse as random factor ignored in simple ANOVA; clustering inflates Type I error.",
    "AD bounded [0,1] violates ANOVA assumptions; ceiling/floor effects possible.",
    "Success binary with high rate (73%) may cause ceiling effects in some mice/conditions.",
    "No information on trial duration, target distance, or maze geometry to normalize metrics."
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Fit linear mixed-effects models with Mouse as random intercept and Stim Paradigm as fixed effect for Time-to-Target, Path Efficiency (log-transformed), Average Speed, and AD (beta regression or transformed). Use generalized linear mixed model (logistic) for Success. Include Mouse × Stim Paradigm random slopes if convergence permits. Report marginal means with 95% CIs, pairwise comparisons with Tukey adjustment, and variance partition coefficients to quantify mouse-level clustering. Conduct sensitivity analyses: (1) exclude extreme Path Efficiency outliers (>10), (2) analyze mouse-level aggregates (n=40 mouse-paradigm combinations) as robustness check."
}
